description: On a `git commit`, checks the commit message and branch name for a ticket reference (task-cli id, GitHub issue #123, Closes/Fixes #N, Linear ABC-123). If none is found and the commit isn't an exempt chore/WIP/merge, it BLOCKS by default (strict) — non-trivial changes should start from a ticket with acceptance criteria + motivation + user-impact. No self-service bypass: request a one-time Telegram approval via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_REQUIRE_TICKET_BEFORE_COMMIT='<justification>' (deny-by-default; bare 1 rejected; consulted BEFORE the `-F -` stdin block so an approved hatch allows a `-F -` commit) — allows only on the human's tg-ctl approval, which is why timeout_ms is 960000. The repo-level REQUIRE_TICKET_STRICT=0 warn-only dial is kept. Enforces the strict-ticket-discipline skill; pairs with task-cli. on_error=open: a CRASH in the check still fails open so a bug never wedges committing — but a successful no-ticket run is a hard block.
